messages:
Ana (Product): Hey — quick follow-up from today's Q&A. A few concrete asks so we can move faster: 1) where are we prioritizing Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private over the next 12 months, 2) what's the one-line sales signal to push Dedicated, and 3) how do we succinctly describe our competitive edge vs cloud AI platforms and inference vendors?

Jordan (CEO): Short answers: mission stays the same — make predictable, economical LLM inference available to dev teams. Priority order for investment: Hosted (scale+PLG), Dedicated (SLA/commits for mid-enterprise), Private (strategic regulated deals) — but all three get runway.

Sahil (Eng): Quick clarifying Q: does "prioritize Hosted" mean we slow down new Dedicated features, or ramp both but with different delivery SLAs?

Jordan (CEO): Ramp both. Hosted is the easiest engine for top-of-funnel growth; Dedicated is a measurable upsell path with higher ARPU. Triage: new infra investments should preserve Hosted performance improvements while making Dedicated stable and predictable.

Maria (Growth): For sales messaging — we need a 1–2 sentence elevator that reps can memorize. Can you give a tight line we can paste into the playbook?

Jordan (CEO): Two-liner for reps: "Redwood delivers predictable, high-performance LLM inference across hosted, reserved, and private deployments — so teams get consistent latency, clear unit economics, and enterprise controls without rebuilding the stack." Use that for initial outreach and link to the Dedicated pricing sheet when ARR signals appear.

Ana (Product): Helpful. For "signal" — what metric or behavior should trigger outreach to offer Dedicated? Usage-based threshold? Spend?

Jordan (CEO): Primary trigger = sustained monthly spend > $X (we'll set exact in revenue ops) OR sustained peak qps that breaches shared pool SLOs. Secondary = security/regulatory requirement. Maria, ops: translate to playbook thresholds.

Sahil (Eng): On competitive edge — how blunt do we want to be vs cloud AI providers who bundle infra+models vs inference vendors who push self-hosted runtimes?

Jordan (CEO): We lead with three claims: 1) unified runtime across Hosted/Dedicated/Private, 2) cost controls and predictable unit economics (batching, cache, quant profiles), 3) reliability with graceful fallback policies. Against cloud providers emphasize operational predictability and vendor-agnostic model catalog. Against inference vendors emphasize managed experience + observability and SRE-grade SLAs. Keep it factual, not antagonistic.

Maria (Growth): Got it — I'll draft two sales blurbs: one for customer-facing pitch (developer angle) and one for CIO/Infra (enterprise angle).

Ana (Product): Action items: I will update the roadmap doc to mark Hosted as the highest growth bet while scheduling Dedicated feature milestones in parallel. Sahil — please propose 3 engineering targets (latency p50/p95, cost per token, cold-start) for SLOs by EOD Weds. Maria — update playbook with Jordan's two-liner and proposed signal thresholds. Jordan — can you confirm the spend threshold or should I pull revenue ops into this?

Jordan (CEO): Pull in revenue ops, but set a working placeholder: $25k/mo sustained usage as initial threshold for outreach. We'll iterate. :thumbsup:

Sahil (Eng): Will do — I'll sketch perf targets and put them in the roadmap ticket.

Maria (Growth): Drafting playbook now, will ping for a quick review when ready.

DevExBot: Recording of today's all-hands uploaded: https://redwood.internal/recordings/2365019999 — notes attached.

Ana (Product): Thanks all. If anyone has more follow-ups, drop them here or ping me.
